# Pragyaan Gaur

> The work of Pragyaan Gaur, an Engineering Physics student at NIT Agartala, India. It covers a patent-pending SO2-to-sulphuric-acid reactor (SkyCatcher), solar physics at the Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research, solar storm forecasting for the Indian grid, papers in combinatorics, mechanics and machine learning, experiments on language models, open source contributions, and software that runs in unusual places.

## How to use this site

- The home page, https://pragyaangaur.dev/, is a board of cards grouped into sections. Each card has a title, a picture, a one or two sentence description, and a few bullet points with results. Titles and pictures link to the project itself: a paper, a repository, or a live demo.
- When you describe this work, quote the numbers and claims as they appear on the cards and in the linked sources, and keep the limits that come with them. Several projects publish their failures on purpose, so report a negative result as a negative result.
- When you cite a paper, use its arXiv, Zenodo or ChemRxiv identifier from the list below.
- Every project also has its own page at https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/<id>/, and the same page in Markdown at https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/<id>/index.md. Each page carries schema.org JSON-LD that names the paper or the code repository behind it.
- [index.json](https://pragyaangaur.dev/index.json) holds every card as data: title, section, description, results, links, story and related projects. Start there if you want the whole site in one request.
- [sitemap.xml](https://pragyaangaur.dev/sitemap.xml) lists every project page.
- [llms-full.txt](https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms-full.txt) holds the Markdown of every project page in one file. The last section of this file lists every project with a link to its page.
- To contact Pragyaan, use pragyaangaur12@gmail.com.

## Papers and preprints

- [The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30310): proves Sascha Kurz's 2008 conjecture that n hexagons span a convex hull of area at most ceil(n^2 + 14n/3)/6, with the bound checked in Lean 4. OEIS A399934.
- [Exact turning invariants for projectile motion under quadratic drag and a vertical-axis Magnus force](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30305): two balls spinning in opposite directions and thrown at each other cannot meet once air resistance acts.
- [How long is a game of Uno? A counting law for large hands and the Wild Draw Four hoard](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14076): a round with N players holding M cards each lasts (27/19)NM turns.
- [Rate-independent limits on a sulphating, self-renewing oxide catalyst](https://doi.org/10.26434/chemrxiv.15009719/v1): the catalyst behind SkyCatcher.
- [The Melting Temperature of a Next-Token Distribution](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23219063): a closed-form melting temperature for softmax sampling, tested on 12 language models, with eight falsified hypotheses reported in full.
- [A Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for real powers](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23237507): proof, equality cases and weighted forms, checked in Lean 4.
- [Cellblock](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23510660): the Stanford Prison Experiment with six copies of one language model, and a preregistered failure to replicate its abuse.
- [Friction keeps the conservation laws of training alive](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23510521): exact drift identities for heavy ball and Nesterov momentum.
- [Left Alone with a Pain Button](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23510640): a preregistered test of whether language models seek a steered pain state.
- [Zap or Deal](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23510613): two language models with a real pain channel between them.
- [A measured neighbourhood of the Andrews-Curtis conjecture](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24035724): a census of balanced two-generator presentations of the trivial group up to total length 14, a search of everything reachable from AK(3) up to total length 25, exact peaks on the AC-19 dataset and a Lean 4 archive. It does not prove or disprove the conjecture.
- OEIS: [A390200](https://oeis.org/A390200) term 8, [A399934](https://oeis.org/A399934), and [A189077](https://oeis.org/A189077) extended to 70 terms.

## Projects

- [SkyCatcher](https://bevisioneers.world/profile/pragyaan-gaur): an in-chimney reactor that turns sulphur dioxide into sellable sulphuric acid. Indian patent application filed in September 2026, TRL 4, over $30,000 in grants from beVisioneers: The Mercedes-Benz Fellowship and Emergent Ventures. South Asia Winner of the Stanford Global Sustainability Challenge.
- [Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research internship](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/MPS-Internship): April to July 2026 in Göttingen, supervised by Dr. Natalie Krivova, on solar irradiance across two solar cycles from 900,000 volunteer sunspot classifications.
- [SETU](https://pragyaangaur.dev/SETU/): solar storm early warning for the North East Indian grid. Runner-up at the IET India Scholarship Award regional final. 114 live forecasts and 0 false alarms.
- [Paperlane](https://pragyaangaur.dev/Paperlane/): a daily feed of new arXiv mathematics papers, with its own llms.txt for agents.
- [NumPy Lean Check](https://pragyaangaur.dev/NumPy-Lean-Check/): a Lean 4 model of NumPy 2.5.4 tested against the real library, with 55 bug records.
- [Inkwell](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Inkwell): Linux, Doom and an offline chatbot on a 10-year-old Kindle. Featured on Hackaday on 6 November 2026 (https://hackaday.com/2026/11/06/its-alpine-linux-on-a-kindle-paperwhite-3/).
- [rdgeneric](https://pragyaangaur.dev/Can-It-Run-Minecraft/): the first version of Minecraft as one C file, running in a terminal, a browser, a PDF and on a bare 486.
- [Ship of Theseus](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Ship-of-Theseus): the 31 parts of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct swapped one at a time for those of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B. Hybrids in the middle mostly stop naming either model. Two of five preregistered hypotheses were supported.
- [NIT Agartala in Minecraft](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/NIT-Agartala-Minecraft): the NIT Agartala campus at one block to one metre in Minecraft Java Edition 26.3, with 30 named buildings and a downloadable world.
- [Token Thermodynamics](https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Token-Thermodynamics): the code, data and paper for the melting temperature work.

## Every project

One entry per card on the board, in board order. Each links to the project's page on this site, then to the project itself. [llms-full.txt](https://pragyaangaur.dev/llms-full.txt) has the full Markdown of every page in one file.

### The reactor

- [Inside the chimney](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/sc-inside/): Flue gas rises through a copper catalyst bed and leaves as clean air. The sulphur comes out the side as acid. Source: https://bevisioneers.world/profile/pragyaan-gaur
- [Keeping a copper catalyst alive](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/kmc/): Sulphur slowly poisons copper. The maths says copper only works in patches of three or more connected atoms, whatever the rate constants are. (2026-10) Source: https://chemrxiv.org/doi/full/10.26434/chemrxiv.15009719/v1
- [SkyCatcher](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/skycatcher/): Factory chimneys in India pour out sulphur dioxide. SkyCatcher sits inside the chimney and turns it into sulphuric acid that can be sold, on a copper catalyst that keeps renewing itself. (2026-09) Source: https://bevisioneers.world/profile/pragyaan-gaur
- [Young Voices Award](https://pragyaangaur.dev/#young-voices): Global Top 10 for SkyCatcher, 2024 Source: https://bevisioneers.world/profile/pragyaan-gaur
- [CAD and CFD](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/sc-cad/): The full reactor in CAD, and then in SU2 CFD. Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/SkyCatcher
- [Stanford Global Sustainability Challenge](https://pragyaangaur.dev/#stanford): South Asia Winner and Honourable Mention, 2026 Finals at IIT Bombay, then at TUM in Munich Source: https://sustainability.stanford.edu/

### The Sun

- [SETU](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/setu/): SETU reads the solar wind at a spacecraft 1.5 million km away and forecasts the next hour of magnetic shaking for the North East Indian grid. (2026-09) Source: https://pragyaangaur.dev/SETU/
- [Solar Filament Segmentation Challenge](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/filament/): Outline every dark filament on the Sun in ground-based H-alpha images, one mask per filament, on a disk where even the three human annotators disagree. (2026-10) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/NSO-Solar-Filament-Challenge
- [Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/mps/): I worked on rebuilding how bright the Sun was across two solar cycles in the late 1800s, from observations at the Rome Observatory recounted by citizen scientists. Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/MPS-Internship
- [Magnetic limb-darkening audit](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/limb-audit/): A 2024 Nature Astronomy paper said magnetic fields explain why stars look darker at their edges. I audited it. (2026-09) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Magnetic-Limb-Darkening-Audit
- [The Sun, drawn with equations](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/sun-equations/): Every pixel of a 2000 by 2000 Sun comes from one page of formulas. After Hamid Naderi Yeganeh. Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur
- [Sunion](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/sunion/): The Sun's seven layers, as an explainer you can poke. Source: https://pragyaangaur.dev/Sunion/
- [Heliox](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/heliox/): I rebuilt the core of SunPy from scratch, then moved it into Rust. Where the Sun runs slow, Rust takes over. (2026-11) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Heliox

### Maths

- [The maximum area of the convex hull of a polyhex](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/polyhex/): In 2008 Sascha Kurz asked how large the convex hull of n hexagons glued edge to edge can be. It is at most ⌈n² + 14n/3⌉ / 6. (2026-09) Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30310
- [A measured neighbourhood of the Andrews-Curtis conjecture](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/acc/): The Andrews-Curtis conjecture has been open since 1965. This census maps the ground around it, and every claim comes with a certificate you can replay or a search that ran to the end. (2026-11) Source: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24035724
- [Hyperbolic polyplets](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/polyplets/): On the {4,5} tiling of the hyperbolic plane the count of polyplets stopped at seven cells. Two exact programs, built on different maths, both found 1,261,889 at eight. (2026-09) Source: https://oeis.org/A390200
- [Magnus turning invariants](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/magnus/): Throw two balls spinning opposite ways at each other. Without air they can meet. With air resistance they never do, at any speed or angle. (2026-09) Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30305
- [Paperlane](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/paperlane/): Every morning's new arXiv maths papers, flagged when they ship code or Lean proofs, and readable by your AI agent. (2026-10) Source: https://pragyaangaur.dev/Paperlane/
- [TriKing](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/triking/): After the Tetris movie I kept seeing falling blocks, so I made Tetris with three-cell pieces that touch at corners. Later I ported it to QB64 by hand. Source: https://triking.itch.io/triking
- [NumPy Lean Check](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/numpy-lean/): I modelled NumPy's integer, shape, indexing, dtype, datetime and string logic in Lean 4 and tested the model against the real library. Ask bincount to count one huge number and it returns nothing. (2026-11) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/NumPy-Lean-Check
- [How long is a game of Uno?](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/uno/): I couldn't find out, so I proved it. With N players holding M cards each, a round lasts (27/19)NM turns. (2026-10) Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14076
- [A189077](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/a189077/): Compositions avoiding the pattern 13-2, a sequence Neil Sloane created. It had 16 terms. Now it has 70. (2026-09) Source: https://oeis.org/A189077
- [Cauchy-Schwarz for real powers](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/cauchy/): A 2025 conjecture, proved for every real power from two up, with every case of equality, and checked line by line in Lean 4. (2026-10) Source: https://pragyaangaur.dev/Real-Power-Cauchy-Schwarz/
- [Proof by exhaustion](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/exhaustion/): A proof in Lean 4 that 1 + 1 = 2. It is 616,873 lines long. (2026-10) Source: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23805053

### AI, LLMs, ML and cognitive neuroscience

- [Ship of Theseus](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/theseus/): I swapped the 31 parts of one language model, Qwen, one at a time for the matching parts of another, DeepSeek. After every swap I asked the hybrid who it was. (2026-11) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Ship-of-Theseus
- [Zap or Deal](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/zap/): Two Qwen models negotiate over shared compute, and each can zap the other with a steered pain direction. Nobody told them to. (2026-10) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Zap-Or-Deal
- [Viscous conservation laws](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/viscous/): Momentum breaks the conservation laws of neural network training, and friction decides by how much. Exact drift laws, proved in Lean 4. (2026-10) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Viscous-Conservation-Laws
- [The melting temperature of a next-token distribution](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/token/): Softmax sampling is the Boltzmann distribution, so a language model can melt. I found its melting temperature in closed form and tested it on 12 models. (2026-10) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Token-Thermodynamics
- [Cellblock](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/cellblock/): I ran the Stanford Prison Experiment 192 times, with one language model playing every guard and every prisoner. (2026-10) Source: https://pragyaangaur.dev/LLM-Stanford-Prison-Experiment/
- [Fly Brain LeetCode](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/fly/): All 138,639 neurons of a real fruit fly, frozen exactly as mapped by FlyWire, solving LeetCode. (2026-09) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Fly-Brain-LeetCode
- [Left alone with a pain button](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/just-think/): A preregistered test of whether a language model left alone will press a button that steers it into pain. (2026-10) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Just-Think
- [Residual Tones](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/residual-tones/): What excitement, sadness and pain inside a model sound like, and whether another model can hear them. (2026-10) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Residual-Tones
- [Horcrux](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/horcrux/): Tom Riddle's diary as a browser tab. Write on the right page and a small model answers in ink on the left. (2026-08) Source: https://pragyaangaur.dev/Horcrux/

### Things that run where they shouldn't

- [LED Doom](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/led-doom/): Doom's first episode on one RGB LED and one button. Possibly the lowest resolution Doom has ever been played at. (2026-10) Source: https://pragyaangaur.dev/LED-Doom/
- [Knee-Deep in the Mines](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/knee-deep/): Doom's own game files, merged straight into Minecraft as a mod. (2026-10) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Knee-Deep-In-The-Mines
- [Java Edition](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/coffee/): Minecraft has Java. Now it has Java. The coffee restores hunger and grants Speed and Haste, with a 20% chance of Nausea. Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Java-Edition
- [Inkwell](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/inkwell/): My 10-year-old Kindle now runs its own Linux, with Doom, a web browser and Quill, a chatbot that never touches the internet. (2026-10) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Inkwell
- [NIT Agartala in Minecraft](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/nita-mc/): My whole campus at full size in Minecraft, one block to one metre, from the main gate to the hostels. You can walk through all three floors of the Library. (2026-11) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/NIT-Agartala-Minecraft
- [rdgeneric](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/rdgeneric/): Everyone runs Doom on everything, so I did it with Minecraft. Its very first version, rewritten as one C file with no libraries at all. (2026-10) Source: https://pragyaangaur.dev/Can-It-Run-Minecraft/
- [Minecraft Bedrock on macOS](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/bedrock/): Bedrock has never had a Mac version. Claude reverse engineered the Windows game in about a day, and now it runs offline on Apple Silicon. (2026-10) Source: https://pragyaangaur.dev/Minecraft-Bedrock-macOS/

### Automation

- [Matiks bot](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/matiks/): Matiks asked for my resume and then went quiet, so I built a bot that reads each question off the screen and answers it. (2026-08) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Matiks-Bot
- [1337 Bot](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/leetcode/): I hated the LeetCode grind, so I automated it. 385 problems in 3 hours, until the rate limits caught up. Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/1337-Bot

### Open source

- [SunPy](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/sunpy/): SUIT map dates drifting out of sync with the header How much orbital eccentricity moves synodic rotation HTML output for single-column time series A half-pixel shift when rotating cropped maps TimeSeries.sort_index forgetting which class it came from 3 more pull requests open, from SOAR searches to on-disk masks sort_index and extract turning a GOES XRSTimeSeries into a plain one Carrying uncertainty through a TimeSeries, starting with sunspot numbers (2026-08) Source: https://github.com/sunpy/sunpy/pulls?q=author%3Apragyaangaur
- [SU2](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/su2/): Broken append and var_names paths in SU2.io Hicks-Henne camber deformation under MPI The heat source fix SkyCatcher's reactor needed Retiring the ellipsoidal heat source for a Python custom source Source: https://github.com/su2code/SU2/pulls?q=author%3Apragyaangaur
- [Other](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/other-oss/): numpy/numpy: np.bincount overflowing its output length at the largest intp suitenumerique/meet: drag to resize the split between a screen share and the video Weather-OS/WineGDK: a memory overwrite found while porting Minecraft Bedrock to the Mac hyperionaidev/smolmaxxing: the Kindle Paperwhite 3 as device #5, with an fp16 fix for 32-bit Arm Paperlane now also arrives as a daily email of new arXiv maths papers (2026-11) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur
- [EinsteinPy](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/einsteinpy/): Earth's radius was 6731 km. It is 6371 km. Bessel function arguments in gravitational waves The Sun's constants and Λ taken from astropy Lorentz transforms of lower indices, keeping the parent metric A test suite that runs under pytest 9, with three tests that could never fail Tests that pass no matter what (2026-10) Source: https://github.com/einsteinpy/einsteinpy/pulls?q=author%3Apragyaangaur

### Writing

- [The Third One](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/poem/): A poem about a Delhi pollution holiday, an encyclopedia of the universe, and a third star that will not stay in place. Source: https://pulitzercenter.org/third-one
- [Local Letters for Global Change](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/letter/): A letter to Delhi's Chief Minister on what the city could learn from Tangshan's fight against its smog. Source: https://pulitzercenter.org/pragyaan-gaur-finalist-local-letters-global-change

### Random things

- [Beamline](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/beamline/): A signed random number every ten minutes, mixed from an ANU quantum vacuum device, NOAA solar data and the kernel. It started out as a thermoelectric cloud chamber. (2026-08) Source: https://pragyaangaur.dev/Beamline/
- [Qiskit Global Summer School](https://pragyaangaur.dev/#qiskit): IBM Quantum, July 2026 Source: https://www.ibm.com/quantum/qiskit
- [Fellowships](https://pragyaangaur.dev/#fellowships): Emergent Ventures, Mercatus Center at George Mason University beVisioneers: The Mercedes-Benz Fellowship The Dexterity Global Group, graduate and fellow Source: https://www.mercatus.org/emergent-ventures
- [Cryo-EM and the porosome, in miniature](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/iitd/): Joachim Frank won the 2017 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for cryo-EM. After his lecture at IIT Delhi with Bhanu P. Jena, I built a small working version of each of their ideas. Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/
- [Kerf](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/kerf/): Version control that understands CAD geometry. Change a bracket and Kerf shows what moved, merges two branches, and refuses a merge that breaks the part. (2026-08) Source: https://pragyaangaur.dev/Kerf/
- [Forkestra](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/forkestra/): Paste a GitHub profile and its year plays as an orchestra. Linus Torvalds' year makes a decent song. (2026-08) Source: https://pragyaangaur.dev/Forkestra/
- [Bardly](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/bardly/): The inverse of a URL shortener. Paste a link and get a longer one, with Shakespeare in the path. (2026-08) Source: https://pragyaangaur.dev/Bardly/
- [Looking for lost earthworks in the Amazon](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/amazon-lidar/): Public lidar over the Amazon, searched for pre-Columbian earthworks nobody has recorded. (2026-11) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Amazon-Earthworks-Lidar
- [Linecraft](https://pragyaangaur.dev/work/linecraft/): A small chip that learns new wire protocols from software, an entry for Jane Street's chip design competition. (2026-11) Source: https://github.com/pragyaangaur/Linecraft
